Keep saved conversation content, memory, strategy material and derived indexes in the active local user profile. Test two distinct user profiles, local backup and recovery, deletion and cache cleanup. Opening one profile or restoring an older copy never reveals the other user’s data or restores an outbound excerpt grant.

plan.outcome: An authorized human or AI change goes through the same Rust registry, survives process restart in the originating local profile and can be undone by operation ID. Accepted results, private records and deletion decisions survive the documented recovery cases. The next slice proves current local human or scoped on-device AI can change the main chart timeframe under independently versioned shared evidence, recover one authorized receipt after a lost response, and undo an eligible chart edit. In the profile-local private-record slice, the owner can explicitly save, list, inspect, correct and delete a titled typed exchange with ordered speakers, a memory or a strategy. The same records reopen after a restart in that profile. A local backup can recover missing records and preserve known deletions.
hypotheses: Start with 1m to 5m, restart the Rust process, undo by the returned operation ID and restart to 1m. Two profiles with the same workspace ID make isolation directly observable.
A profile-bound, long-lived Rust core can share one transaction owner across the native and explicitly enabled Ubuntu workspace entries.

A synthetic original thesis and a separately dated outcome can be distinguished after restart. Deleting their note can retain a profile-bound marker and redacted operation results without leaving the body available to a live read, undo or idempotent replay.
A logical backup limited to decision notes can recover missing originals and dated outcomes, keep newer work, and suppress marked notes without copying operation history, grants or SQLite journals.

Restore stages can retain only pending inserts and release them when the revision changes, a deadline expires or the session ends. Revision-based projection refresh can preserve a surviving note's unsubmitted outcome draft while clearing deleted list entries and details.

The published single-series CSV revision UUID identifies the frozen chart and scopes its instrument identity. Derive the history-chain-v1 hash from the exact stored bars. Use the exclusive bar-start coverage bound as the deterministic cutoff for this closed-bar source, which carries no observation clock.

Native publication browsing can use stored v5 revision summaries while v6 selection and projected chart reads continue through scoped workspace permissions. Opening a library row follows the same revocation checks as opening by revision ID.

An already submitted deletion can retain only its original scope, challenge and opaque record ID after the detail disappears. Retry recovers the original body-free receipt or returns a current terminal denial. Exercise a dropped committed reply, BUSY during post-commit WAL cleanup, and BUSY before commit followed by a peer rename using actual Chromium and SQLite.

Two real browser windows sharing a workspace must clear unavailable private bodies and invalid reviews. If a peer corrects a record that remains authorized, preserve the local draft and explicitly review it against the current record. Independent pending approvals on one writer are bounded and cancellation is scoped to the exact challenge. Restore reports all current surviving records, including those absent from the archive.

A private records panel reachable from the native and enabled Ubuntu workspace serves all three types through one typed read and write contract. Manual capture keeps existing transient conversation and speech flows independent.
A bounded logical private-record archive can merge missing records and the union of known tombstones without retaining prior bodies, outbound grants or a secondary search index.

Use the workspace revision and the selected record revision for correction and deletion. A revision-bound local approval stages only the pending changes. Committing and replaying use a random challenge with no private body or fingerprint in the approval request, log or receipt. The state-migrations gate runs the persistence suite without a name filter. It covers genuine v1–v7 fixtures, rollback and reopen, private archive recovery, deletion cleanup and refusal of restored approval or outbound access.

evolution.data_plan: Keep application state inside the bound OS-user profile. The v1 to v2 migration retains chart state, undo and replay and adds immutable originals, separate outcomes and profile-scoped deletion markers. The reference restores no disclosure grant. Add v8 with a bound private-record table, body-free replay metadata and tombstones. Use one SQLite transaction for the workspace revision, receipt and record change. The logical archive retains current record bodies and tombstone IDs only.
evolution.cleanup: Delete original and outcome bodies, clear body-derived replay fingerprints, and durably resume SQLite WAL cleanup if a reader blocks it. Restore without replaying past AI work or reusing external disclosure grants. Clear the selected reference explicitly without resetting its token. Deny a revoked target without restoring or exporting its contents. Securely replace or delete superseded private record bodies and checkpoint SQLite WAL with durable retry. Release browser drafts and approval stages on cancel, supersession and close. Warn about independent older copies.

A defined release-candidate lifecycle can reuse existing acceptance gates while packaging and publication remain future product work.
